quests.instruction: Who checks a bus's brakes and fixes its engine in a garage?
quests.hint: They use spanners and know how engines work.
quests.explanation: A mechanic repairs and services vehicles so they run safely. Regular check-ups find small problems before they become big ones.
quests.funFact: Many mechanics use computers to read messages from a vehicle's sensors.

quests.instruction: Who builds and mends the roads, bridges, and railway tracks that vehicles travel on?
quests.hint: They wear hard hats and bright vests at work sites.
quests.explanation: Construction workers build the roads, bridges, and tracks that vehicles rely on. Without them, travel would be much slower and harder.
quests.funFact: Road crews often work at night so there is less traffic to disturb.

quests.instruction: Who drives a tractor to plough fields and bring in the harvest?
quests.hint: Their job is growing food.
quests.explanation: Farmers use tractors, trailers, and trucks to grow crops and move them. Machines help one farmer look after a very large field.
quests.funFact: Some modern tractors use satellite signals to drive in perfectly straight lines.

quests.instruction: What do we call a person who rides a bicycle along the road or a cycle lane?
quests.hint: Two wheels and two pedals are the clue.
quests.explanation: A cyclist is a road user who rides a bicycle. Cyclists follow traffic rules like everyone else and wear a helmet for protection.
quests.funFact: In some cities, cyclists have their own traffic lights.

quests.instruction: A person taps a long white cane along the pavement to feel the way ahead. Which person is this?
quests.hint: The long cane helps them feel kerbs and obstacles.
quests.explanation: Someone using a white cane may be blind or have low vision. Drivers should wait patiently and give extra time when they cross.
quests.funFact: Some traffic lights beep to tell people who cannot see when it is safe to cross.

quests.instruction: Which passenger needs a special rear-facing seat fixed in the car for protection?
quests.hint: This passenger is too small for an ordinary seat belt.
quests.explanation: Babies and small children need seats made for their size. A properly fitted child seat protects them far better than a normal belt.
quests.funFact: Many countries have laws that require babies and young children to travel in child seats.

quests.instruction: A bus is crowded and an older person is standing, holding on tightly. Who should you offer your seat to?
quests.hint: Standing on a moving bus is harder for some people than others.
quests.explanation: Offering a seat to an older person, someone who is hurt, or someone carrying a baby is kind and helps them stay safe.
quests.funFact: Many buses and trains have seats reserved for people who need them most.

quests.instruction: At the end of a train ride you have an empty snack wrapper. Where should it go?
quests.hint: Look for the container made for rubbish.
quests.explanation: Putting rubbish in a bin keeps stations and vehicles clean and safe. Litter on the floor can make people slip.
quests.funFact: Many stations have separate bins for paper, plastic, and general rubbish.

quests.instruction: On a quiet train, people nearby are trying to sleep or read. Which is the polite way to talk?
quests.hint: Think about what helps others rest.
quests.explanation: Speaking softly and using headphones shows respect for others. Shared transport works best when everyone is considerate.
quests.funFact: Some trains have quiet carriages where passengers are asked to keep noise low.

quests.instruction: Who rides in the back of an ambulance and gives patients treatment on the way to hospital?
quests.hint: They have medical training and carry a first-aid kit.
quests.explanation: A paramedic is trained to treat injuries and illness in emergencies. They care for patients before they reach the hospital.
quests.funFact: Some paramedics ride bicycles or motorbikes to reach crowded places quickly.

quests.instruction: The traffic lights at a busy crossroads have stopped working. Who might step into the road to guide the cars safely?
quests.hint: They wear a uniform, and drivers must follow their hand signals.
quests.explanation: Police officers or trained traffic wardens can direct traffic with hand signals. Drivers must obey them to keep everyone safe.
quests.funFact: Officers use clear hand signals so drivers can understand them without words.

quests.instruction: Which trained helper wears a special harness and guides a person who cannot see across the road?
quests.hint: It has had months of special training and works as a loyal helper.
quests.explanation: A guide dog leads its owner around obstacles and stops at kerbs. People should never distract a guide dog while it is working.
quests.funFact: Guide dogs go through months of training before they begin their work.

quests.instruction: A plumber must carry pipes, tools, and spare parts to different homes all day. Which vehicle suits the job?
quests.hint: It needs a roomy space for tools and must be small enough to park outside houses.
quests.explanation: A van holds tools and spare parts while still fitting along ordinary streets. Many tradespeople use vans for their work.
quests.funFact: Many tradespeople have their business name printed on the side of their van.

quests.instruction: A gardener needs to haul bags of soil, long hedge-cutters, and plants. Which vehicle with an open back would work well?
quests.hint: It has a flat, open area behind the seats.
quests.explanation: An open back is handy for bulky or muddy loads that you would not want inside a car.
quests.funFact: Open loads should always be tied down so nothing falls out on the road.

quests.instruction: Some villages have no library. Which vehicle can travel round with shelves of books and bring them to the people?
quests.hint: It has lots of space inside for shelves and visitors.
quests.explanation: A mobile library is a bus fitted with shelves. It visits villages on a timetable, so people can borrow books.
quests.funFact: Some mobile libraries travel to remote places by boat or even by camel.

quests.instruction: A bus breaks down on a quiet road. What can the driver use to call for help?
quests.hint: It can make calls and send messages.
quests.explanation: A mobile phone lets drivers and passengers call for help or tell others they will be late. It is one of the most useful things to carry on a journey.
quests.funFact: Many phones can share your location, so helpers can find you faster.

quests.instruction: You are lost in a big station. Who sits at the information desk to answer questions?
quests.hint: Look for the desk with a question-mark sign.
quests.explanation: Station staff can tell you which platform to use and how to find your train. Asking for help is a smart way to avoid getting lost.
quests.funFact: Big stations and airports often have information desks and screens in several languages.

quests.instruction: Who often teaches children how to cross the road safely at school?
quests.hint: This person works in a classroom.
quests.explanation: Teachers and road-safety officers show children how to stop, look, and listen before crossing. Practising helps good habits stick.
quests.funFact: Many schools invite police officers or road-safety teams to give talks about staying safe.

quests.instruction: At crowded festivals, some police officers patrol on which animal so they can see over the crowd?
quests.hint: It is tall and fast and wears a saddle.
quests.explanation: Mounted police can see far over a crowd and move through it calmly. Horses are trained to stay steady in loud places.
quests.funFact: Police horses train for months to stay calm around noise and crowds.

quests.instruction: Long ago, people trained certain birds to fly home carrying small notes. Which bird is shown?
quests.hint: It has white wings and is often a symbol of peace.
quests.explanation: Homing pigeons can find their way home from far away, so people used them to send messages before phones existed.
quests.funFact: Homing pigeons have found their way home from hundreds of kilometres away.

quests.instruction: Where do you drop a letter so postal workers can collect it and send it on its way?
quests.hint: It has a slot for letters.
quests.explanation: Letters in a post box are collected, sorted, and sent by road, rail, or air. The address on an envelope tells the postal system where it must go.
quests.funFact: Post boxes in different countries come in different colours, such as red, blue, or yellow.

quests.instruction: Which is the very first step of a train journey: buying a ticket, riding the train, or arriving?
quests.hint: You do this before the train even arrives.
quests.explanation: A journey has steps: plan, buy a ticket, travel, and arrive. Having a ticket ready means you can board without delay.
quests.funFact: Many travellers buy tickets online before they reach the station.

quests.instruction: Before pulling away, a driver usually needs this to switch on the car's engine. What is it?
quests.hint: It is small and jingles in your pocket.
quests.explanation: A car key, or a key fob, tells the car that the right person is starting it. It helps keep the car from being driven by someone else.
quests.funFact: Many modern cars start with a button as long as the key fob is nearby.

quests.instruction: Before a long trip in an electric car, what should the driver make sure is charged?
quests.hint: It stores the power that turns the wheels.
quests.explanation: An electric car runs on stored electricity. Charging before a long journey and planning stops helps the trip go smoothly.
quests.funFact: Charging can take about half an hour at a fast charger, or a whole night at home.

quests.instruction: Who should always hold an adult's hand when crossing a busy road?
quests.hint: This person is small and still learning road safety.
quests.explanation: Young children can misjudge speed and distance. Holding a grown-up's hand keeps them safe while they learn to cross.
quests.funFact: Drivers often cannot see small children who are behind parked cars.

quests.instruction: A bus has a clear, flat space with a special sign. Which passenger is it mainly for?
quests.hint: This passenger travels in a seat that has big wheels.
quests.explanation: The space is for people who use wheelchairs. Keeping it free means they can travel safely and comfortably.
quests.funFact: Many buses can lower or tilt, or use ramps, to make boarding easier.

quests.instruction: Every weekday morning, many children choose whether to walk, cycle, or take a bus to which place?
quests.hint: It has classrooms and a playground.
quests.explanation: Travelling to school is a daily journey for many children. Walking and cycling build healthy habits, while buses help children who live farther away.
quests.funFact: In some places, 'walking buses' are groups of children who walk to school together with adult helpers.

quests.instruction: A mechanic finds that the rubber a car rolls on is worn smooth and slippery. Which round part needs replacing?
quests.hint: This is the part that grips the road, especially when it is wet.
quests.explanation: Tyre treads grip the road, especially when it is wet. Worn tyres cannot grip well, so a mechanic replaces them.
quests.funFact: Tyre treads have patterns of grooves that push water out of the way.

quests.instruction: A car's front light is broken and it is getting dark. What should a mechanic replace?
quests.hint: It is the part that helps the driver see ahead.
quests.explanation: Working lights help drivers see and be seen. A car with a broken headlight is unsafe to drive at night.
quests.funFact: Many modern cars use LED lights, which last a long time.

quests.instruction: A town crossroads has had many near-misses. What could the town add to help traffic take turns?
quests.hint: It changes colour to tell drivers when to go.
quests.explanation: Traffic lights give each road a turn, which helps prevent crashes. Planners study busy crossings to decide where lights are needed.
quests.funFact: Some traffic lights have sensors that notice when vehicles or walkers are waiting.
